title: Composing Task-specific Agent Harnesses at Test Time with Reusable Primitives
title_zh: 在测试时利用可复用原语组合任务专用 Agent Harnesses
abstract_en: Agent harnesses govern how large language models (LLMs) gather context, invoke tools, verify results, preserve state, and terminate, largely affecting agent performance. However, the value of each harness mechanism can differ across heterogeneous tasks: a mechanism that improves one task may impose overhead or context distraction on another, leading to the suboptimality of a global harness. We characterize this suboptimality as a mismatch induced by fixed mechanism choices, motivating task-specific harness construction. Nonetheless, generating harness code for each task introduces generation and debugging costs, with execution risks that can compound as more mechanisms are generated. To address those challenges, we introduce Harness Primitives, reusable harness mechanisms with clear application scope and composition contract mined from failed task trajectories. Based on Harness Primitives, we propose STITCH, a framework that Selects suitable primitives given Task Information and compiles them into Task-speCific Harnesses at test time. This separation enables task-specific harnesses without generating or repairing mechanism code at test time. Extensive experiments demonstrate that STITCH not only improves harness adaptability and robustness, but also scales with the primitive library size, boosting task success rates by up to 12 points over fixed harness baselines, surpassing human-designed harnesses like Codex CLI while maintaining a minimal test-time harness composition overhead of only 2.7%, 638 times more efficient than generating task-specific harnesses from scratch. Ultimately, our work demonstrates that building task-adaptive harnesses can be beneficial for completing diverse tasks and that building reusable primitives can be a promising path towards this goal.
abstract_zh: Agent harnesses 负责控制大语言模型（LLM）如何收集上下文、调用工具、验证结果、保存状态与终止执行，对智能体性能有重要影响。然而，不同任务对各类机制的需求不同，固定的全局 harness 可能引入额外开销或上下文干扰，造成机制选择不匹配。为此，论文提出 Harness Primitives：从失败任务轨迹中挖掘具有明确适用范围与组合契约的可复用 harness 机制。基于此，作者提出 STITCH（Selects suitable primitives given Task Information and compiles them into Task-speCific Harnesses），在测试时根据任务信息选择合适原语，并编译为任务专用 harness。该方法避免了测试时生成和修复 harness 代码，降低了执行风险与调试成本。实验表明，STITCH 能提升 harness 的适应性与鲁棒性，并随原语库规模扩展而持续受益；相比固定 harness，任务成功率最高提升 12 个百分点，超过包括 Codex CLI 在内的人类设计 harness，同时测试时组合开销仅为 2.7%，效率比从零生成任务专用 harness 高 638 倍。
key_points_zh: 固定 harness 在异构任务上存在机制选择不匹配，可能带来无效开销和上下文干扰。
Harness Primitives 从失败轨迹中提炼可复用机制，并通过适用范围与组合契约支持安全组合。
STITCH 在测试时依据任务信息选择原语并编译任务专用 harness，无需生成或修复机制代码。
实验中 STITCH 相比固定 harness 最高提升 12 个百分点的任务成功率，并超过 Codex CLI。
测试时组合开销仅 2.7%，较从零生成任务专用 harness 的方案高效 638 倍。

llm_assessment.comment: STITCH presents a highly reusable harness architecture that composes mined primitives into task-specific workflows without costly test-time code generation.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: STITCH提出了高度可复用的Harness架构，可将挖掘出的原语组合成任务专用工作流而无需昂贵的测试时代码生成。
